hood_desc: A laid-back beachside area on Denpasar's east coast with a calm lagoon, boardwalk, older resorts and expat cafes; suits families, older travelers and those wanting a mellow seaside base.
Denpasar's spacious government and diplomatic district, leafy and orderly with the Bajra Sandhi monument and jogging parks; suits business visitors and those wanting quiet, upscale local living.
A busy central-south Denpasar neighborhood, local and residential with markets, guesthouses and street food; suits budget travelers wanting authentic city life.
A traditional eastern Denpasar area rich in temples and Balinese family compounds; suits culture seekers wanting an authentic residential and spiritual atmosphere.
A growing residential south-central neighborhood with cafes, co-working spots and easy access to Renon and Sanur; suits digital nomads and longer-stay visitors wanting local convenience.

water.note: Avoid tap water; use bottled, boiled, or filtered water throughout your stay.

transit.pay: Pay onboard with cash or a QRIS e-wallet scan for a flat fare of about Rp 4,400 (~$0.30) per ride. Coverage is limited, so most visitors instead use the Grab or Gojek apps for on-demand cars and scooters, typically Rp 15,000-40,000 (~$1-3) per short trip.
transit.hours: Buses run approximately 5am-9pm with no night service; Grab/Gojek ride-hailing operates 24 hours.
transit.note: Bali is best navigated with Grab/Gojek and scooter or car rentals; Trans Metro Dewata buses are a budget option mainly for fixed corridors around Denpasar, Sanur and Kuta.

landmarks: Bajra Sandhi Monument
A towering bell-shaped monument in Puputan Margarana Park depicting Balinese history, iconic for its ornate carved exterior.
Puputan Badung Square
A historic public square and park commemorating the 1906 Puputan battle, marked by dramatic bronze statues.
Jagatnatha Temple
Bali's largest state temple, notable for its tall white coral-stone padmasana shrine set in a lotus pond courtyard.
Bali Museum
A traditional Balinese palace-style museum complex whose ornate gateways and pavilions showcase classic island architecture.
Sanur Beach
A calm, palm-lined eastern coastline within Denpasar famous for tranquil sunrise views over the water.
Maospahit Temple
One of Bali's oldest temples, distinguished by its Majapahit-era red-brick relief carvings rarely seen elsewhere on the island.
Taman Werdhi Budaya Art Centre
A cultural complex with traditional Balinese pavilions and an open-air amphitheater used for dance and art performances.
Badung Market (Pasar Badung)
Bali's largest traditional market, a colorful multi-level hub of produce and crafts popular for vibrant street photography.
Kumbasari Market
A riverside handicraft market facing Badung Market, connected by a pedestrian bridge over the Badung River, a scenic local scene.
Blanjong Pillar (Prasasti Blanjong)
A rare 10th-century inscribed stone pillar in Sanur, one of the oldest historical inscriptions found in Bali.

train.note: Bali has no railway at all. The nearest trains are on Java, run by KAI (https://www.kai.id/) - you would cross by ferry from Gilimanuk to Ketapang and pick up trains at Banyuwangi or Surabaya.

bus.note: Bali is an island, so there are no international buses. State operator DAMRI (https://damri.co.id/) runs long-distance domestic coaches, including a Jakarta-Denpasar service (launched March 2026) plus routes to Surabaya and Yogyakarta, using the Gilimanuk-Ketapang ferry crossing.

ferry.note: No scheduled international passenger ferries run from Bali. Domestic crossings go from Gilimanuk (West Bali) to Ketapang on Java, operated by ASDP Indonesia Ferry (https://www.indonesiaferry.co.id/), and from Padangbai to Lombok and the Gili/Nusa islands.
